title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.isIso_boundedConstructibleBaseChange_of_isProper
statement: For a prime ℓ, a finite normed field extension E of Q_ℓ, and separated finite-type schemes X,Y,X′,Y′ over a field k of positive prime characteristic different from ℓ, let f,g,f′,g′ be k-morphisms forming a cartesian square with f proper. The bounded constructible pro-étale base-change natural transformation for the condensed ring C(-,E), Rf_* followed by Lg^* to Lg′^* followed by Rf′_*, is an isomorphism of functors.

proof.text: For the four given separated finite-type $k$-schemes apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Its hypotheses are exactly the prime $\ell$, finite normed extension $E$, positive prime characteristic unequal to $\ell$, and the stated scheme conditions. Obtain the equivalences $J_X,J_Y,J_{X'},J_{Y'}$, their essential surjectivity, and comparisons of the four pullbacks and direct images. In particular the source and target functors in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] restrict to the bounded constructible categories actually used by the archived declaration; the integral rationalized categories are not being identified with them by notation.

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] to this cartesian square with $f$ proper and an arbitrary object $M$ in its rationalized source category. It gives invertibility of the rational exchange $e_M:Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}^*Rf_{\mathrm{rat},*}M\to Rf'_{\mathrm{rat},*}Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}'^*M$. These are exactly the rational functors appearing in the realization comparison, rather than the condensed-module functors presumed equal to them. No restriction on $g$ is used.

source.place: isIso_boundedConstructibleBaseChange_of_isProper; reduction described in the module docstring, realized via Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14(2) and 6.8.15

proof.text: The final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] identifies the specified rationalized completed exchange with the adjunction mate; this is a substantive comparison input, rather than an inference from equivalence of categories alone. Identify the morphism, not just its endpoints. The archived map is the three-step composite in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Under the comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], its first factor is the image of the rational unit at $Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}^*Rf_{\mathrm{rat},*}M$, its middle factor is the image of the pullback-composition comparison for $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$, and its last factor is the image of the rational counit at $M$, whiskered by $Rf'_{\mathrm{rat},*}Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}'^*$. Preservation of composition by $J_{Y'}$ now gives $\mathrm{BC}_{J_XM}=b_M\circ J_{Y'}(e_M)\circ a_M^{-1}$, where $a_M:J_{Y'}Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}^*Rf_{\mathrm{rat},*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_c^*Rf_{c,*}J_XM$ and $b_M:J_{Y'}Rf'_{\mathrm{rat},*}Lg_{\mathrm{rat}}'^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{c,*}Lg_c'^*J_XM$ are the comparison composites. Cancellation of adjacent comparison inverses in the unit, square and counit factors is the asserted equality.

source.place: isIso_boundedConstructibleBaseChange_of_isProper; reduction described in the module docstring, realized via Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14(2) and 6.8.15

proof.text: The component at $J_XM$ has inverse $a_M\circ J_{Y'}(e_M^{-1})\circ b_M^{-1}$; functoriality and the two inverse identities for $e_M$ verify both composites are identities. For arbitrary $K$ choose $u:J_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ using essential surjectivity from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Naturality gives $\mathrm{BC}_K=B(u)\circ\mathrm{BC}_{J_XM}\circ A(u)^{-1}$ for the two endpoint functors $A=Lg_c^*Rf_{c,*}$ and $B=Rf'_{c,*}Lg_c'^*$, so every component is invertible. The component inverses form a natural transformation: $B(v)\mathrm{BC}_K=\mathrm{BC}_{K'}A(v)$ implies $A(v)\mathrm{BC}_K^{-1}=\mathrm{BC}_{K'}^{-1}B(v)$ by composing with inverses on both sides. They therefore give an inverse to the specified natural transformation, proving the exact functor isomorphism required.
